subject: Infosec discovery and next steps for PayBridge — evidence & DPA path
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@paybridge.com>, security@paybridge.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Infosec discovery and next steps for PayBridge — evidence & DPA path

Hi Lisa / PayBridge security team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the clear framing of your compliance constraints. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the priority asks from your side, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Quick summary of pain & goals
- Pain: unpredictable token-level costs + lack of auditability for customer-submitted PII in our current hosted provider; regulatory requirement to retain audit logs for payment flows.
- Goal: move to an inference setup that provides deterministically retained audit logs, clear data residency, and a DPA that accepts 7-year retention for transaction metadata.
- Risk tolerance: medium — PayBridge requires SOC 2 Type II evidence and pen test results before production rollout.

What we confirmed during the call
- SOC 2: You want our SOC 2 Type II report and a short readiness summary for the specific controls covering encryption-in-transit, key management, and logging.
- Audit logs / retention: Primary requirement is retention of request/response audit logs for up to 7 years, with the ability to export on demand. You also asked for retention policy enforcement and deletion proof for non-production datasets.
- Pen test: You will require a third-party pen test and a vendor acceptance matrix; scope includes network edge, authentication flows (SAML/OIDC), and model hosting isolation.
- DPA & redlines: Your legal team will serve redlines on the DPA; we discussed the main points (retention, breach notification timing, subprocessor disclosures).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Infosec evidence checklist (owner: me) — I attached an initial checklist (infosec-evidence-checklist.xlsx). I will populate the SOC 2 artifacts we can share and mark any attestations that require an NDA or on-site review. ETA: 2027-11-18 EOD.
2) DPA redlines (owner: PayBridge legal; action: send redlines) — you mentioned a redline set from your counsel. Please send by 2027-11-19 so we can triage.
3) Pen test scope & vendor (owner: PayBridge security) — please confirm scope and preferred vendor by 2027-11-24; we can provide a test environment or an isolated Dedicated capacity for the exercise.
4) Short follow-up call to align on final artifact list and timelines (owner: Karthik / Neha). Proposed slot: 2027-11-22 or 2027-11-23.

Potential blockers and mitigations
- If your legal requires changes to our data processing terms beyond standard DPA templates, that can extend procurement; we recommend parallel technical readiness to avoid blocking go-live.
- For retention beyond our standard 2 years, we may need an addendum specifying storage tiering and cost implications; I’ll run numbers with our pricing team once you confirm 7-year retention is required for all audit artifacts versus a subset.

Attachments: infosec-evidence-checklist.xlsx, dpa-redlines-20271110.pdf (our internal starting point).

Please let me know if I missed anything important. Happy to adjust the checklist with your security contacts.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime
From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@paybridge.com>

Cc: security@paybridge.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Infosec discovery and next steps for PayBridge — evidence & DPA path

On Tue, Nov 16, 2027 at 2:12 PM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the clear framing of your compliance constraints. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the priority asks from your side, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Thanks Neha — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Retention: 7 years applies to transaction metadata (headers, timestamps, non-PII routing info). For full request/response payloads that include cardholder data or PAN we will require tokenization or vaulting — we will not accept raw PAN retention. If Redwood can provide field-level redaction or allow routing those fields to our vault, that satisfies this requirement.
- SOC 2 artifacts: please include the cover letter and the control matrix mapping to the sections we discussed (CC6, CC7 equivalents for cloud services). If you can mark which artifacts are redacted because they contain customer data, that helps speed our review.
- Pen test: We intend to run the vendor through our procurement and will propose a vendor list by 2027-11-19. For the Dedicated capacity option, we need network diagrams and ACL rules before scheduling.

We will send initial DPA redlines to security@paybridge.com by COB 2027-11-19.

Two quick asks for your team before the follow-up call:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-customer encryption keys (CMKs) and whether those keys are customer-managed via KMS/HSM?
2) Do you have an artifact that documents log export and immutability guarantees (WORM or equivalent)?

I’ll bring these items up with our security lead. If it helps, schedule the follow-up for 2027-11-22 10:00 PT and Karthik can run a short demo of the logging controls.

—Lisa
Lisa Gomez
Director, InfoSec 
PayBridge
lisa.gomez@paybridge.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@paybridge.com>, security@paybridge.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Infosec discovery and next steps for PayBridge — evidence & DPA path

Lisa — thanks for the quick clarifications, very helpful. Short answers up front, then confirmed next steps with owners and dates.

Short answers
- CMKs / customer-managed keys: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed CMKs via major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). We can enable a customer-managed key per workspace. I attached a pointer to our KMS integration notes in the Drive link.
- Log export & immutability: We provide an audited export path to an S3/GCS bucket with object-lock (WORM) support; our retention enforcement is policy-driven and we can generate tamper-evident checksums on export. I’ll add the specific artifact to the checklist.

Confirmed next steps (updated)
- Neha: Finalized evidence checklist (populate SOC 2 artifacts + mark redacted items) — ETA: 2027-11-18 EOD — attached.
- PayBridge security: DPA redlines to security@paybridge.com — ETA: 2027-11-19 COB.
- PayBridge security: Pen-test vendor list + scope; request network diagrams/ACLs if you want Redwood test environment — ETA: 2027-11-19.
- Karthik: Logging demo + brief on Dedicated test environment (includes network diagram & ACL example) — scheduled for 2027-11-22 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent).
- Marissa: Pricing estimate for 7-year audit log retention (owner: Marissa) — ETA: 2027-11-20.

Attachments & links
- infosec-evidence-checklist.xlsx (updated)
- dpa-redlines-20271110.pdf (our starting template)
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-4821
- Security pack: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPayBridgeInfosecPack

If PayBridge is comfortable with the above, we’ll treat the DPA redlines as the gating legal item and run the technical evidence concurrently so we can move to a pilot soon after.

Thanks — talk Thursday.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
